newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady on Tuesday supported by abbreviated flour mill times this holiday week but burdened by continued slow demand, dealers said.

"Very little has changed as far as demand is concerned but we will see a little less (flour mill) runtime due to the upcoming holiday," a Buffalo dealer said. "Most markets will lose some time because of Easter."
One Kansas dealer said the fact that livestock producers have started putting animals out on pastures in parts of Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas will reduce demand for middlings.
"If the weatherman cooperates, grass and fieldwork hit at about the same time and they both lessen demand," he said.
"We are getting green grass, so that is another factor," a North Carolina broker said.

"There is nothing happening. Luckily, I have nothing much to sell," a Minnesota dealer said. But he noted grain markets were up, which pressure those players who want to switch to corn rather than midds.
"Midds are competitive to corn," he said. "Everytime we have a strong grains market, it does not hurt the midd prices. At least they hold."
